title: Hygiene with limited water
label: FOOD & HYGIENE
deck: Reserve safe water for drinking, food, medicines and essential hygiene. Wash hands with safe water and soap before food preparation and after toilet or waste handling. Keep clean and dirty tasks separate. Sanitiser with at least 60% alcohol helps when hands are not visibly dirty; it does not remove chemicals or replace washing dirty hands.
tldr: Reserve safe water for drinking, food, medicines and essential hygiene. Wash hands with safe water and soap before food preparation and after toilet or waste handling. Keep clean and dirty tasks separate. Sanitiser with at least 60% alcohol helps when hands are not visibly dirty; it does not remove chemicals or replace washing dirty hands.
steps: Put safe water, soap and a clean towel or air-drying arrangement near food and care tasks. Use a container that does not require everyone to dip dirty hands into the supply.
Wash after toilet and waste handling, before eating or preparing food and before wound or infant care. Do not use suspected chemically contaminated water on skin.
Use at least 60% alcohol sanitiser when soap and safe water are unavailable and hands are not visibly dirty. Keep it away from flames and children.
Store rubbish and toilet waste away from water, food and sleeping areas. Clean high-contact surfaces using product instructions without mixing chemicals.
Include menstrual supplies, nappies, necessary skin care and clean clothing. Keep wounds clean and covered; worsening redness, pain or fever needs medical assessment.
next: Replenish safe water when a verified source becomes available. Keep a routine that the household can sustain; a simple clean station is more useful than occasional improvised deep cleaning.
watch: Surface disinfectant is not drinking-water treatment. Do not apply household bleach to skin or mix bleach with ammonia or other cleaners.
without_help: Use the smallest workable clean-water station and protect it from contamination. Reduce nonessential washing before cutting drinking water or essential handwashing.
household: Make the hygiene plan usable for children, mobility needs and caregivers changing diapers or handling wounds. Keep gloves, cleaning tools and drinking-water supplies distinct. Tell everyone where the clean handwashing area is and who manages waste.
pack_now: Suitable water, soap, a stable dispenser, a clean drying method, required personal-care items and separate containment for soiled materials. Keep cleaning-product labels readable and away from food.

faqs: No. CDC notes that sanitizer has limits, including visibly dirty or greasy hands and harmful chemicals. Plan suitable water and soap, especially around toilet, waste and meal tasks.
Can I use water that is unsafe to drink for bathing?
Sometimes an advisory allows certain non-drinking uses, but it depends on the contaminant and notice. Follow the specific permission; do not infer it from a different incident.
scope: Civilian educational guidance. Linked references may use U.S. emergency systems; local warning methods, laws, services and conditions differ.

blocks.text: When water, drainage, and rubbish collection fail, hygiene is a household system rather than a bottle of sanitizer. Decide where clean drinking water and food stay, where people wash hands, where personal care happens, and how waste is contained. Keep these activities separate enough that a dirty container, glove, or cloth cannot routinely pass through the meal area.

blocks.caption: A simple hygiene workflow
items: Keep safe water, food, clean care items, and utensils protected.
Use an accessible dispensing point with appropriate water and soap, and a suitable way to handle runoff.
Keep contained waste and soiled materials separate; wash hands before returning to clean tasks.
blocks.note: Editorial layout concept. It is not a plumbing or waste-disposal design; local water and sanitation restrictions still apply.

blocks.text: In a small dwelling, separation may mean labelled containers, a dedicated changing surface, and a sequence that is easy to follow rather than different rooms. Choose a stable setup the least mobile person can use. Keep walking routes clear, particularly at night. Waste should not be placed where children or pets can access it.

CDC advises washing hands with soap and water for at least 20 seconds. Important times include after toilet use or handling waste and before preparing or eating food. Check the actual water advisory to determine whether tap water is acceptable for handwashing; a drinking restriction and a do-not-use restriction are different.

blocks.caption: Match the method to the conditions
rows: Suitable water and soap available
Use proper handwashing and a clean drying method.
No normal running tap
Set up a stable jug dispenser with appropriate water; avoid shared dipping into the supply.
Soap and water unavailable
CDC identifies sanitizer containing at least 60% alcohol as an alternative in some situations.
Visibly dirty or greasy hands
Sanitizer is less effective; obtain soap and appropriate water.
Possible chemical contamination
Sanitizer may not remove harmful chemicals; follow exposure guidance rather than assuming it decontaminates.

blocks.text: Keep soap and a light beside the station rather than in a separate cupboard. Plan where runoff goes; do not use drains affected by sewage failure. Teach the setup to children with suitable supervision and arrange assistance for anyone who cannot operate the dispenser. Empty or unstable equipment creates a station that exists on paper but not in practice.

sections.heading: Use limited water for essential personal care

blocks.text: Choose suitable water for brushing teeth and follow the local notice for bathing. Do not bathe in water potentially contaminated with sewage or toxic chemicals. Reduced bathing can be a practical temporary adjustment, but necessary handwashing, oral care, and provider-directed care still need a plan.

items: Keep each person’s toothbrush, hygiene items, and drying materials identifiable; do not make several people share a dirty cloth.
Plan menstrual supplies, continence care, skin care, and privacy explicitly rather than calling all of these “toiletries.”
Record special water or cleaning requirements from an individual care plan. A general household routine does not replace those instructions.
Keep wounds protected from contaminated water, and seek medical help for signs of infection or other concerning change.
Separate pet cleanup from human meal and personal-care surfaces.

blocks.text: Estimate water used by an actual routine rather than making an arbitrary ration. Try a safe practice while normal water remains available: locate supplies, operate the dispenser, and complete the usual essential tasks. Use the observed amount to improve the reserve. Never withhold necessary drinking water or prescribed care to make a target last longer.

sections.heading: Diapering and assisted care need their own setup

blocks.text: Prepare a dedicated, cleanable changing area away from food. Bring the required items before starting so the child is not left unattended while a caregiver searches. Follow CDC’s diaper-changing sequence, including separating soiled items, washing the child’s hands, cleaning and disinfecting the surface as directed, and washing the caregiver’s hands.

Use an appropriate product for the surface and follow its label, including any contact time. Disposable gloves, when used, do not replace handwashing. Keep clean diapers, wipes, spare clothes, and bagging materials within reach, while putting the closed used-item container where children cannot reach it. Adult continence care also needs dignity, a stable position, privacy, and any individual skin-care instructions.

blocks.title: Plan the whole care cycle
blocks.text: A stack of clean diapers is only one part of the plan. Include the changing space, handwashing water, cleaning supplies, soiled-clothing containment, waste route, and a backup caregiver if needed.

If a caregiver must also prepare meals, make the transition explicit: finish the dirty task, contain used items, clean as directed, wash hands, then return to clean supplies. Do not put a changing mat on the only meal-preparation surface just because it is convenient.

Cleaning removes visible soil; disinfecting uses a suitable product as directed to address germs. Product type, surface, and instructions matter. Do not mix cleaning chemicals or improvise concentrated recipes. A chemical label must be readable and the product kept out of drinking-water containers.

blocks.caption: An editorial cleaning checklist
rows: Identify the surface and contamination
Ordinary household dirt, a changing surface, and sewage contamination need different responses.
Choose a suitable product
Read the label for permitted surfaces, dilution, precautions, and contact time.
Prepare the work area
Keep food, people needing care, and pets away from the dirty task.
Handle used materials
Keep soiled cloths and waste separate from clean supplies.
Finish safely
Wash hands and restore clean supplies without recontaminating them.

blocks.text: Significant sewage contamination may require qualified cleanup and an alternative living space. Do not treat a quick wipe or a splash of bleach as proof that a contaminated room is safe. Keep electrical and structural hazards in view, and avoid entering unsafe water to begin cleaning.

sections.heading: Maintain the routine and know its limits

blocks.text: Record suitable water, soap, personal-care consumables, liners, and the functioning waste route. Review actual use and replenish before the routine fails. A supply of waste bags does not establish that collection exists or that every type of waste can go into ordinary rubbish. Follow the relevant local disposal arrangements.

items: Check the station at the start of the day: water, soap, light, stability, and runoff arrangements.
Check each person’s essential personal-care needs and the supplies they can actually use.
Keep clean and used materials separated, and supervise children appropriately.
Record any service or advisory change and adjust the routine.
If safe water, care, or waste containment cannot be sustained, arrange a suitable alternative location early.

blocks.text: After normal service returns, confirm the appropriate water and drainage instructions, clean affected equipment as directed, and replenish the hygiene kit. Note one preventable difficulty: a missing soap dispenser, an inaccessible container, inadequate privacy, or an unconfirmed waste route. Fixing that difficulty can provide more value than buying another generic emergency pouch.
